citations.title: Legal Authority
citations.requirement: Rules are adopted under O.C.G.A. § 31-7-300 et seq.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Defines: applicant/licensee by entity type (.03(b)); companion or sitter tasks (.03(c)); home management, where any employee with unlimited access to client funds must be bonded through the provider (.03(g)); medically frail or compromised client (.03(j)); medically related activities, including reminding clients to take medication and assisting with self-administration, but excluding professional services (.03(k)); owner as any person with 10% or greater interest (.03(l)); personal care tasks (.03(n)); private home care provider and services (.03(o)-(p)); transport and escort, which requires a client waiver of claims or reasonable efforts to confirm motor vehicle insurance when the employee drives a vehicle not owned by the client (.03(s)).

citations.title: Governing Body
citations.requirement: Each provider must have a governing body empowered and responsible to determine all policies and procedures and to ensure compliance with the rules.

citations.title: Licenses
citations.requirement: No operation without a license or provisional license (.05(1)). Owner must comply with Chapter 111-8-12 before a new license issues (.05(1)(b)). A provisional license may be issued to a new provider for a limited time or to an existing provider with an acceptable plan of improvement (.05(1)(c)). Administrator and employees must be qualified (.05(2)). Each location is separately licensed (.05(2)(a)). The license must be displayed (.05(2)(b)). It is not assignable or transferable. It must be returned on change of name, location, ownership or governing body. DCH must get 15 days' advance notice of a location change (.05(2)(c)).

citations.title: Applications
citations.requirement: Initial application on DCH forms, with application fee, Board-set license fee, owner records check application, and description of services and geographic area (.06(1)). Periodic renewal with a description of services and area (.06(2)). Fees are reasonable and may be refunded for good cause (.06(3)). Applications must be truthful. DCH may refuse a license for false statements (.06(4)).

citations.title: Exemptions
citations.requirement: Rules do not apply to an individual who personally provides services without agents, employees, contractors or financially interested referrals (.07(1)(a)), nor to licensed home health agencies (.07(1)(d)) or personal care home staff (.07(1)(e)). No Certificate of Need is required for a PHCP-only license (.07(2)).

citations.title: Inspections and Plans of Correction
citations.requirement: Periodic inspection, with possible exemption for accredited providers (.08(1)). Application or renewal is consent to entry during regular business hours, and DCH gets access to premises, records, staff and consenting clients (.08(2)). Staff must cooperate without unreasonable delay (.08(3)). An acceptable written plan of correction is due within ten days of receiving the written report. The provider may explain or dispute findings in the plan (.08(4)).

citations.title: Administration and Organization — Services Description
citations.requirement: Written policies and procedures must define the scope of services offered and the types of clients served. No service prohibited by the rules or other law may be provided.

citations.title: Administration and Organization — Service Agreements
citations.requirement: Do not offer services you cannot reasonably deliver. Written policies are required. All services are based on a written agreement with 10 required elements (.09(2)(a)1-10), including referral and contact dates, services, frequency, charges and billing, receipt of rights notice, the provider's phone number, the DCH phone number, authorization for client funds or vehicle use, and signatures. The agreement must be completed by the 2nd visit if on a different day than the 1st, or within 7 calendar days of first service, whichever is earlier (.09(2)(b)). Good-cause delay must be documented (.09(2)(b)1). Later changes are documented in the record as agreed by the client (.09(2)(b)2). The client may cancel at any time and pays only for services rendered. Only a reasonable travel and staff-time charge is allowed if the staff member has already arrived (.09(2)(c)).

citations.title: Administration and Organization — Administrator
citations.requirement: The governing body appoints an administrator with full authority and responsibility for operations. Qualifications: no credible evidence of abuse, neglect, exploitation or deprivation; participation in required orientation and training; no material false statements. The current SOS text of (3)(a)1 also requires a satisfactory fingerprint records check determination. See the notes on version conflict.

citations.title: Record keeping — Client Records
citations.requirement: A separate file per client containing: identifying information; current service agreement; current service plan; signed nursing notes if nursing is provided; documentation of personal care and companion/sitter tasks actually performed; supervisory visit findings; material reports and communications; physician contacts; date and source of referral.

citations.title: Retention and Confidentiality of Client Records
citations.requirement: Written policies must state who supervises records, who has custody, to whom and why records are released, and how long they are retained. Minimum retention is five years from the last service. Disclosure is allowed only to appropriate staff, the client, the responsible party, the client's physician or other provider, DCH, persons authorized in writing by the client, or by subpoena.

citations.title: Personnel Records
citations.requirement: A separate record per employee containing: identifying and emergency contact information; 5-year employment history; qualifications; satisfactory TB screening at hire and annually; date of employment; job description; orientation and training documentation; at least an annual performance evaluation; bonding documentation if the employee has unlimited access to client funds (a universal bond is acceptable).

citations.title: Reports of Complaints and Incidents
citations.requirement: Keep files of all complaints under .12(2). Keep incident reports and reports of unusual occurrences (e.g., falls, accidents, significant medication errors) for at least five years. Documentation must show actions taken to resolve complaints and address incidents.

citations.title: Staffing — General and Nursing Personnel
citations.requirement: Keep sufficient qualified staff for the service agreements. On an unexpected staff shortage, advise the client and refer to another provider if the client wishes. Staff must have a written competency evaluation by direct observation or demonstration. Hires must have no credible evidence of abuse or exploitation, must complete orientation and training, and must make no false qualification statements. Nursing personnel must hold a Georgia license.

citations.title: Personal Care Assistant (PCA) Qualifications
citations.requirement: A PCA must have one of: a nurse aide program under 42 CFR Part 483 Subpart D; a DCH-recognized nurse aide competency exam; a DCH-approved health care or personal care credential; or a 40-hour provider training program covering ambulation and transfer, personal care tasks, first aid and CPR, special conditions, home management, home safety and sanitation, infection control, medically related activities and vital signs, and nutrition. The 40-hour program must be directed by an RN or an equivalent professional. 20 hours must be completed before serving clients and the other 20 within six months of starting. No PCA may be assigned a task without completed training and a competency determination. No PCA may care for a client with special conditions without training and demonstrated competency.

citations.title: Companions or Sitters
citations.requirement: Companions or sitters may perform only companion or sitter tasks unless also qualified as a nurse or PCA. They must read, write, follow instructions and complete reports. They must be trained or competent in the needs of elderly, handicapped or convalescing persons, meal preparation, transport and escort, housekeeping and sanitation, home safety, handling medical emergencies, and infection control.

citations.title: Staff Training
citations.requirement: Orientation before working with clients must cover: written policies on scope of services and client types; client rights and complaints (.12); the employee's duties; reporting client progress and problems and handling medical emergencies and incidents; and the duty to report known exposure to TB or hepatitis. Each employee must receive at least 8 clock hours of training annually after the first year of employment, in subjects relating to their duties.

citations.title: Contracted Services
citations.requirement: Contractor arrangements must be in writing and detail the services. The provider must ensure the contractor follows the rules and is qualified. The services must be supervised under .10(2) by a supervisor of the licensed provider.

citations.title: Categories of Services
citations.requirement: Nursing services are delivered by an RN or LPN under a supervisor. Personal care tasks are performed by a qualified PCA (or nurse) per the service plan. Companion or sitter tasks are performed by a qualified companion or sitter per the service plan. PCAs, companions and sitters must report client needs, changes in condition and observed problems.

citations.title: Supervision of Services; Nursing Supervision
citations.requirement: Qualified staff must supervise all services. Each staff member must be evaluated in writing at least annually by direct observation or demonstration. No supervisor may knowingly permit an employee who has been exposed to or diagnosed with TB or hepatitis to serve clients until the employee is determined not to be contagious. A provider offering nursing must employ a fully licensed Georgia RN supervisor.

citations.title: Supervision of Personal Care Tasks
citations.requirement: Supervisors must be qualified by education, training and experience. A licensed RN or LPN must supervise personal care for medically frail or compromised clients. An RN must complete the initial service plan for those clients. A supervisory home visit to the client's residence is due at least every 92 days from the date of initial service, or sooner as the level of care requires. The visit assesses general condition and vital signs, progress, problems, client satisfaction and appropriateness of services, and is documented in the client file or plan.

citations.title: Supervision of Companion or Sitter Tasks
citations.requirement: A qualified supervisor (RN, LPN, the administrator or another assigned staff member) completes the service plan. A supervisory home visit is due at least every 122 days from initial service, or when a complaint raises a serious question about services. The visit assesses condition, progress, problems, satisfaction and appropriateness of services, is made in the residence, and is documented.

citations.title: On-call Representative for Medically Frail Clients
citations.requirement: When staff perform personal care for medically frail or compromised clients in their homes, a provider representative must be on call and able to reach a nurse supervisor by phone or other means to consult with staff on the clients' medical needs.

citations.title: Documentation of Home Care Services Provided
citations.requirement: Written policies must provide for documenting the services actually performed each day. The documentation goes into the client file under .09(4)(a).

citations.title: Quality Improvement Program
citations.requirement: Maintain documentation of an effective quality improvement program that continuously monitors program performance and client outcomes against standards of care and the rules. At minimum, document receipt and resolution of complaints, problems with care identified, and corrective actions.

citations.title: Service Plans
citations.requirement: Written policies are required. The plan is developed with the client, the responsible party, and the physician if nursing is provided. Content: functional limitations, services, times and frequency, duration, goals and objectives, and discharge plans. Where applicable it also covers diagnoses, medications and treatments, equipment, and diet. The service supervisor completes the plan within seven working days after services start. Nursing plans are reviewed and updated at least every 62 days. Other plans are reviewed at each supervisory visit and revised when the content items change.

citations.title: Client Rights, Responsibilities, and Complaints
citations.requirement: A written notice of rights and responsibilities must be given when the service agreement is completed. It covers 11 items (.12(2)(a)-(k)): participation in planning, being informed of changes, accepting or refusing services, charges, the supervisor's name and contact, complaint procedures and non-retaliation, confidentiality, respect for property and residence, DCH address and phone, a copy of the most recent inspection report on written request (after the plan of correction is filed, with a reasonable copying charge), and the client's duty to report changes in condition. Also required: oral or written complaint procedures with timely resolution (.12(3)), and giving the provider's phone number for information, questions and complaints (.12(4)).

citations.title: Enforcement and Penalties
citations.requirement: After notice and an opportunity for hearing, DCH may refuse, limit, restrict, suspend, revoke or refuse to renew a license, issue a public reprimand, or impose a fine.

citations.title: Rules and Regulations for Criminal Background Checks
citations.requirement: The owner must comply before a new PHCP license is issued (per .05(1)(b)). Which positions beyond the owner and administrator are covered was not verified; confirm with HFRD.

citations.title: In-Home Services
citations.requirement: CCSP in-home service providers must hold a current, valid DCH private home care license.

citations.title: Georgia Elderly and Disabled Waiver (CCSP/SOURCE)
citations.requirement: 1915(c) waiver approved 11/09/2022 to 11/08/2027. DCH handles reimbursement, enrollment and utilization review, and DAS runs day-to-day CCSP operations.

citations.cite: 21st Century Cures Act (2016) § 12006 — EVV; Georgia DCH EVV program
citations.title: Electronic Visit Verification
citations.requirement: EVV is required for Medicaid-financed personal care services. Georgia's system is Netsmart Mobile Caregiver+. Each visit records service type, recipient, provider, date, location and start/end times. Waiver billing: CCSP/SOURCE (IDs 590/930) T1019 with TF/UC; ICWP (660) and NOW/COMP (680/681) T2025.

citations.title: Reporting of need for protective services
citations.requirement: Persons with reasonable cause to believe a disabled adult or elder person has been abused, neglected or exploited must report to the designated adult protection agency (DHS-DAS Adult Protective Services) and to an appropriate law enforcement agency or prosecutor. A staff member of a hospital, social agency, financial institution or similar facility must notify the person in charge, who reports or causes the report. Any other person may report. Good-faith reporters are immune (§ 30-5-4(c)). The statute's list of mandated reporters was seen only in part; the agency's policy treats every caregiver as a reporter.

citations.title: Third-party employers of home care workers
citations.requirement: Per the provided research: third-party employers (agencies) may not claim the companionship exemption from overtime. The 2026 status of this section was not confirmed, so verify before finalizing the overtime policy.

policies.title: Governing Body Authority, Policy Approval and Annual Review
state_specifics: The governing body is empowered and responsible for determining all policies and procedures and for ensuring compliance with Rule 111-8-65.
When a corporation or LLC owns the provider, the entity is the licensee and its governing body acts.
The governing body appoints the administrator (Rule .09(3)).
All policies are approved by the governing body, with an approval date and version.
Review the manual at least annually and whenever DCH amends Rule 111-8-65. Check the 2026 revision and the HB 183 independent contractor change.

policies.title: Scope of Services, Types of Clients Served and Acceptance of Clients
state_specifics: Written scope lists the services offered: personal care tasks and/or companion or sitter tasks. Nursing is offered only if an RN supervisor is employed.
The policy states which client types are served and whether medically frail or compromised clients are accepted.
Never provide a service prohibited by the rules or other law, and never accept a client whose services cannot reasonably be delivered.
Staff may not perform tasks outside the scope in the service plan.

policies.title: Service Agreement Content (10 Required Elements)
state_specifics: Every client gets a written agreement with the client or responsible party. It includes the date of initial contact and the date of referral.
It includes the services requested, the services to be provided, expected frequency and duration, and the charges with billing and payment mechanics.
It includes the client's acknowledgment of receipt of the Rule .12 rights and responsibilities, the provider's phone number, and the DCH phone number.
It includes authorization for access to client funds (bill paying, shopping) and for use of the client's vehicle, where applicable.
Signatures and dates from the provider representative and the client or responsible party. If the client refuses to sign, note the refusal and an explanation on the agreement.

policies.title: Service Agreement Timing, Revisions and Client Cancellation
state_specifics: Complete the agreement by the 2nd visit (if on a different day than the 1st) or within 7 calendar days of first service, whichever is earlier.
If the agreement cannot be completed for good cause, document the reason in the client file.
Later changes (service, frequency, duration, charge) are noted in the record as discussed with and agreed to by the client or responsible party before the change takes effect.
The client may cancel at any time and pays only for services actually rendered before notice.
A reasonable travel and staff-time charge is allowed only if the caregiver has already arrived. No minimum-hour or non-cancellable terms.

policies.title: Administrator Appointment and Qualifications
state_specifics: The governing body appoints an administrator with full authority and responsibility for operations.
The administrator must obtain a satisfactory fingerprint records check determination under Chapter 111-8-12 (current SOS text; an older version lacks this wording).
The administrator participates in the required orientation and training and makes no material false statements about qualifications.
No credible evidence of abuse, neglect, exploitation or deprivation.
Name a back-up person to act when the administrator is absent.

policies.title: Client Record Contents
state_specifics: Keep a separate file per client with 9 items: identifying information and responsible party; current service agreement; and current service plan.
Also keep signed and dated nursing/progress notes if nursing is provided; documentation of personal care and companion/sitter tasks actually performed; and supervisory visit findings.
Also keep material reports and communications (employee problem reports, physician, family or responsible party), physician names and phone numbers, and the date and source of referral.

policies.title: Client Record Security, Retention, Confidentiality and Release
state_specifics: The policy names who supervises records, who has custody, to whom and why records are released, and how long they are kept.
Retain client records at least 5 years from the date of last service.
Release only to appropriate provider staff, the client, the responsible party, the client's physician or other provider, DCH, persons authorized in writing by the client, or by subpoena.
Employees may not disclose or knowingly permit disclosure outside those categories.

policies.title: Personnel Records and Employee Health Screening
state_specifics: A separate file per employee: identifying and emergency contact information; 5-year employment history; qualifications; and health screening records.

Also: date of employment; job description; orientation and training documentation; at least an annual performance evaluation; and bonding documentation if the employee has unlimited access to client funds (a universal bond is acceptable).
The health screening program covers initial, routine and targeted screenings of employees and contractors.
TB: screen before starting work per CDC guidance for baseline screening of health care personnel. The agency also re-screens annually, as the prior rule text required, until confirmed otherwise.
Staff report known exposure to TB or hepatitis. No supervisor may knowingly let an exposed or diagnosed employee serve clients until determined not contagious.

policies.title: Staffing Sufficiency and Unexpected Staff Shortages
state_specifics: Keep enough qualified staff to deliver the services in every service agreement.
If the agency learns it cannot deliver the services because of an unexpected staff shortage, advise the client and refer them to another provider if they wish.
Document the notice and referral in the client file.
Do not accept new clients when caregiver capacity does not exist.

policies.title: Hiring Qualifications and Written Competency Evaluation
state_specifics: Before serving as a direct access employee, obtain a satisfactory fingerprint records check determination under Chapter 111-8-12.
Each employee has a written competency evaluation, with the supervisor observing job tasks by demonstration or direct observation, in the personnel file.
Hires complete required orientation and training and make no material false statements about qualifications.
Verify with HFRD which positions beyond the owner, administrator and direct access employees need fingerprint checks.

policies.title: Nursing Personnel Licensure
state_specifics: Any person hired to provide nursing services must hold a Georgia license (RN or LPN).
Verify the license with the Georgia nursing licensing board at hire and at each renewal.
Nurses may also perform personal care and companion/sitter tasks.
Do not advertise or provide nursing unless an RN supervisor is employed.

policies.title: Personal Care Assistant (PCA) Qualifications and 40-Hour Training Program
state_specifics: PCAs may perform personal care and companion/sitter tasks, but not nursing.
A PCA needs one of: a 42 CFR 483 Subpart D nurse aide program; a DCH-recognized nurse aide competency exam; a DCH-approved credential; or the 40-hour provider program.

The 40-hour program covers ambulation and transfer, personal care tasks, first aid and CPR, special conditions, home management, home safety and sanitation, infection control, medically related activities and vital signs, and nutrition.
An RN or equivalent professional directs the program. 20 hours are done before serving clients and 20 within 6 months of the training start date.
No task is assigned until training and competency are documented. No special-conditions client is assigned without specific training and demonstrated competency.

policies.title: Companions and Sitters
state_specifics: Companions or sitters perform only companion or sitter tasks unless also qualified as a nurse or PCA.
They must read and write, follow verbal and written instructions, and complete reports.

Training or demonstrated competency is required in: needs of elderly, handicapped or convalescing persons; meal preparation and serving; transport and escort; housekeeping and sanitation; home safety; medical emergencies; infection control.
Document training or the competency demonstration in the personnel file.

policies.title: Orientation Before Working With Clients
state_specifics: Orientation is completed before any client contact.
Content: policies on scope of services and client types; client rights and complaints (Rule .12); the employee's assigned duties and responsibilities.
Also: reporting client progress and problems to supervisors; handling medical emergencies and incidents; the duty to report known exposure to TB or hepatitis.
Keep a signed orientation checklist in the personnel file.

policies.title: Annual In-Service Training (8 Clock Hours)
state_specifics: A minimum of 8 clock hours of training per employee per year after the first year of employment.
Topics must relate to the employee's assigned duties.
Track hours and topics by employee.
Employees hired before the rule's effective date also need 8 hours annually.

policies.title: Contracted Services and Independent Contractors
state_specifics: Any independent contractor, individual or agent providing services on the agency's behalf needs a written arrangement detailing the services.
The agency must ensure the contractor follows the rules and is qualified.
A supervisor of the licensed agency supervises contracted services under Rule .10(2).
The agency policy is to employ aides as W-2 employees. The proposed HB 183 revision would limit contractors to Title 43 licensed professionals; adoption status is unverified.

policies.category: Rule .10 Private Home Care Provider Services
policies.title: Nursing Services and RN Supervisor
state_specifics: Offered only if the agency employs a fully licensed Georgia RN to supervise nursing services and the employees providing them.
Nursing is performed by an RN or LPN within the scope of nursing practice and the service plan.
Nursing services: regularly assess needs, take part in the service plan, provide nursing per the plan, and report problems and progress to the supervisor or the client's physician.
The RN supervisor completes the service plan with the staff who will deliver care.

policies.category: Rule .10 Private Home Care Provider Services
policies.title: Personal Care Tasks
state_specifics: Personal care tasks (bathing, toileting, grooming, shaving, dental care, dressing, eating) are performed by a qualified PCA or a licensed nurse.
Work is under a supervisor and per the service plan.
The PCA reports personal care needs, changes in condition and observed problems.
Never perform tasks outside the service plan or beyond training.

policies.category: Rule .10 Private Home Care Provider Services
policies.title: Companion or Sitter Tasks
state_specifics: Companion or sitter tasks (transport and escort, meal preparation and serving, household tasks essential to cleanliness and safety) are performed by a qualified companion, sitter, PCA or nurse.
Work is under a qualified supervisor and per the service plan.
The companion or sitter reports client needs, changes in condition and observed problems.
Companions may not provide personal care or nursing.

policies.category: Rule .10 Private Home Care Provider Services
policies.title: Supervision of Services, Annual Written Evaluation and Exposure Exclusion
state_specifics: Qualified staff of the agency supervise all services.
Each staff member is evaluated in writing at least annually, by direct observation or demonstration of their job tasks.
No supervisor knowingly permits an employee who has been exposed to or diagnosed with TB or hepatitis to serve clients until determined not contagious.
File evaluations in the personnel record.

policies.category: Rule .10 Private Home Care Provider Services
policies.title: Supervision of Personal Care Tasks and Medically Frail or Compromised Clients
state_specifics: Personal care supervisors must be qualified by education, training and experience.
A licensed RN or LPN supervises personal care for clients determined medically frail or compromised. An LPN reports to an RN who stays responsible for the service plan.
An RN completes the initial service plan for medically frail or compromised clients. An LPN may make later revisions, which the RN reviews in a timely manner.
The policy defines how the agency determines whether a client is medically frail or compromised, and documents the determination at intake.

policies.category: Rule .10 Private Home Care Provider Services
policies.title: Supervisory Home Visits — Personal Care Clients (Every 92 Days)
state_specifics: A supervisory home visit to the client's residence at least every 92 days from the date of initial service, or sooner as the level of care requires.
The visit assesses general condition and vital signs, progress, problems, client satisfaction and appropriateness of the level of services.
Document the visit in the client file or service plan.
The provided research cites 122 days for personal care; the verified rule text (.10(2)(b)) says 92 days. The agency uses 92 days for personal care clients and checks the live rule text.

policies.category: Rule .10 Private Home Care Provider Services
policies.title: Supervision of Companion or Sitter Services and 122-Day Home Visits
state_specifics: A qualified supervisor (RN, LPN, administrator or another assigned staff member) supervises companion or sitter tasks and completes the service plan.
Supervisory home visit at least every 122 days from initial service, or sooner when a complaint raises a serious question about services.
The visit assesses condition, progress, problems, satisfaction and appropriateness of services.
Visits are made in the residence and documented in the client file or service plan.
Clients who receive any personal care tasks follow the 92-day schedule in SVC-06.

policies.category: Rule .10 Private Home Care Provider Services
policies.title: On-Call Representative for Medically Frail or Compromised Clients
state_specifics: While staff or subcontractors provide personal care to medically frail or compromised clients in their homes, a provider representative must be on call and accessible.
That representative can reach a nurse supervisor by phone or other means to consult on the client's medical needs.
Publish an on-call roster and the after-hours number to caregivers.
Log on-call consultations.

policies.category: Rule .10 Private Home Care Provider Services
policies.title: Daily Documentation of Services Performed
state_specifics: Document the services actually performed for each client each day.
Documentation goes into the client file under Rule .09(4)(a).
Caregivers document tasks, not just the schedule. Supervisors review the notes at each supervisory visit.
Medicaid clients also need EVV data that matches the daily notes.

policies.category: Rule .10 Private Home Care Provider Services
policies.title: Quality Improvement Program
state_specifics: Maintain documentation of an effective program that continuously monitors program performance and client outcomes against standards of care and Rule 111-8-65.
Minimum records: receipt and resolution of complaints, problems with care identified, and corrective actions taken.
Review the QI log with the governing body at least quarterly.
Include audits of supervisory visit timeliness, service agreement timing and personnel file completeness.

policies.title: Service Plan Development, Content and Review
state_specifics: Develop the plan with the client, the responsible party and, for nursing services, the client's physician.

Content: functional limitations, services, times and frequency, duration, goals and objectives, and discharge plans. Where applicable it also covers diagnoses, medications and treatments, equipment, and diet.
The service supervisor completes the plan within 7 working days after services first begin in the residence.
Nursing plans are reviewed and updated at least every 62 days.
Other plans are reviewed at each supervisory visit and revised when the content changes.

policies.category: Rule .12 Client Rights, Responsibilities, and Complaints
policies.title: Client Rights and Responsibilities and Written Notice
state_specifics: Give the written notice of rights and responsibilities to each client or responsible party when the service agreement is completed.
The notice covers the right to be informed about and take part in planning the service plan, and the right to be promptly informed of plan changes.
It covers the right to accept or refuse services, and the right to be fully informed of charges.
It includes the client's duty to report changes in condition.
The client acknowledges receipt in the service agreement (Rule .09(2)(a)6). Medicaid HCBS clients also get the waiver program's rights notices.

policies.category: Rule .12 Client Rights, Responsibilities, and Complaints
policies.title: Complaints and Grievances; Supervisor Contact Information
state_specifics: Inform the client of the name, business phone and business address of the person supervising services and how to reach them.
Complaints may be oral or written, with no discrimination or retaliation. The provider investigates within a reasonable period of time.
Name the complaint handler with business address and phone in the client notice.
Record every complaint and its resolution, and feed them into the QI program.
Tell clients that unresolved licensing complaints can go to DCH.

policies.category: Rule .12 Client Rights, Responsibilities, and Complaints
policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Clients have the right to confidentiality of their record.
Disclosure is limited to the categories in Rule .09(4)(b)2.
Name a privacy officer, and train all staff at hire.
Caregivers do not discuss clients on social media or with non-staff.
Breach response and notification follow 45 CFR 164 Subpart D if the agency is a covered entity (Medicaid billing).

policies.category: Rule .12 Client Rights, Responsibilities, and Complaints
policies.title: Respect for Property, Client Funds, Gifts, Bonding and Exploitation Prevention
state_specifics: Clients have the right to have property and residence treated with respect.
Any employee with unlimited access to client personal funds for home management must be bonded through the agency (a universal bond is acceptable).
Access to client funds requires written authorization in the service agreement.
No caregiver may accept gifts, loans, bequests or add themselves to client accounts.
Report suspected financial exploitation under SAF-01.

policies.category: Rule .12 Client Rights, Responsibilities, and Complaints
policies.title: DCH Contact Notice and Copy of Inspection Report
state_specifics: Give each client written notice of the DCH address and phone, explaining that DCH licenses the provider and investigates complaints that appear to violate licensing rules.
On written request, give the client a copy of the most recent completed licensure inspection report. Provide it after the plan of correction is filed; a reasonable copying charge applies.
The DCH phone number is also required in the service agreement.
Confirm the rest of .12(2)(j) and any later items against the live rule text. The retrieved excerpt was cut off.

policies.category: Rule .12 Client Rights, Responsibilities, and Complaints
policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
state_specifics: Do not discriminate in accepting or serving clients or hiring staff on any protected basis.
Provide interpreters or translated notices at no charge.
Offer the rights notice, service agreement and complaint procedures in accessible formats.
Make reasonable accommodations for clients and employees with disabilities.

policies.title: Licensure, Location, License Display, Advertising and Notice of Changes
state_specifics: No operation without a DCH license or provisional license. No Certificate of Need is needed for a PHCP-only license.
Each office location is licensed separately, and the license must be displayed at the licensed location.
The license is not assignable or transferable. Return it on a change of name, location, ownership or governing body.
DCH must receive 15 days' advance notice of a location change.
Advertise only services actually offered and licensed, and the service area stated in the application. Do not advertise nursing without an RN supervisor.

policies.title: Applications, Renewal, Fees and Truthful Statements
state_specifics: Use DCH forms. Initial application includes the application fee, the Board-set license fee, the owner records check application, and the description of services and geographic area.
All licensure fees must be paid in full before the license is issued. DCH's checklist lists a $300 application processing fee, non-refundable; confirm the current amount on the DCH form.
Renew periodically with an updated description of services and area. Calendar the renewal date with HFRD.
Applications must be truthful. DCH may refuse a license for false statements.
The owner (10% or greater interest) must satisfy Chapter 111-8-12 before a new license issues.

policies.title: DCH Inspections and Plans of Correction
state_specifics: Application or renewal is consent to entry during regular business hours. Give DCH access to premises, records, staff and consenting clients.
Staff cooperate without unreasonable delay.
Submit an acceptable written plan of correction within 10 days of receiving the written report. The provider may explain or dispute findings in the plan.
Assign one person to receive DCH mail and calendar the deadline the day the report arrives.
Keep an inspection-ready binder: personnel files, training records, sample agreements.

policies.title: Enforcement Actions, Sanctions and Hearing Rights
state_specifics: After notice and an opportunity for hearing, DCH may refuse, limit, restrict, suspend, revoke or refuse to renew a license, issue a public reprimand, or impose a fine.
The administrator notifies the governing body within one business day of any DCH notice of sanction.
Follow the hearing request deadline on the DCH notice.
Keep a log of all enforcement correspondence.

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
state_specifics: Bill only for services actually delivered and documented, with matching EVV data for Medicaid.
Screen employees against the OIG exclusion list before hire and monthly.
Referral arrangements must follow anti-kickback rules. Under Rule .07(1)(a), an individual with financially interested referrals is not exempt.
Staff may report concerns without retaliation; the compliance officer investigates.
Medicaid waiver providers must hold a current DCH PHCP license (DAS HCBS 5300 Manual § 208).

policies.title: Required Reports and Notices to the State
state_specifics: Report to DCH: location change (15 days' advance notice), change of name, ownership or governing body, and renewal applications.
Plan of correction due 10 days after the written inspection report.
Abuse, neglect and exploitation reports go to DHS-DAS Adult Protective Services and law enforcement (O.C.G.A. § 30-5-4).
Medicaid program reports and incident reporting follow each waiver program's requirements.
Calendar all report due dates in a compliance log.

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Every employee is treated as a reporter. Anyone with reasonable cause to believe a disabled adult or elder has been abused, neglected or exploited reports to DHS-DAS Adult Protective Services and to law enforcement or a prosecutor (O.C.G.A. § 30-5-4).
Report to the person in charge as well; that does not replace the individual's duty to report.
Good-faith reporters are immune. No retaliation.
Confirm the statute's reporting timing and current APS intake number before finalizing, and post the number for staff.
Remove an accused employee from the client pending the investigation.

policies.title: Incident and Unusual Occurrence Reporting
state_specifics: Document all incident reports and unusual occurrences (falls, accidents, significant medication errors) that affect client health, safety or welfare.
Keep them on file at least 5 years.
Documentation shows the actions taken to address each incident.
Keep complaint files under Rule .12(2) with actions taken to resolve.
Caregivers report incidents to the supervisor immediately and complete the written report the same day.

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Infection control in the home is part of PCA training and companion/sitter competency.
Staff report known exposure to TB or hepatitis. The exposed employee is excluded from client care until determined not contagious.
Provide gloves and personal protective equipment.
Follow CDC-based screening for employees (see ADM-07).
Offer hepatitis B vaccination where OSHA applies.

policies.title: Client Emergency and Disaster Plans
state_specifics: Orientation covers handling medical emergencies and incidents (Rule .09(6)(a)3).
Assess each client's emergency and evacuation needs at intake and note them in the service plan.
Keep an on-call representative and a way to contact a nurse supervisor for medically frail clients (SVC-08).
Prepare for severe weather, power loss and hurricane evacuation; call clients before and after events.

policies.title: Caregiver Safety in the Home and Workplace Violence
state_specifics: Orientation includes home safety.
Caregivers may leave an unsafe home and call the supervisor.
Report workplace violence and harassment without retaliation.
Document hazards found at the supervisory home visit.
Provide safe lifting and transfer training.

policies.title: Transporting Clients and Use of Vehicles
state_specifics: Transport and escort is offered only if listed in the scope of services.

If an employee drives a vehicle not owned by the client, get a signed waiver of claims by the client, or make reasonable efforts to confirm current motor vehicle insurance with medical coverage for the client.
Use of the client's own vehicle needs written authorization in the service agreement (.09(2)(a)9).
Check the driver's license and carry hired and non-owned auto coverage.
Document the waiver or insurance proof in the client file.

policies.title: Change in Client Condition and Emergencies in the Home
state_specifics: PCAs and companions must report client needs, changes in condition and observed problems (Rule .10(1)).
Call 911 first for life-threatening emergencies, then the supervisor.
The supervisor notifies the responsible party and physician and updates the service plan.
Clients must report changes in their condition (rights notice).
Document in the client file and complete an incident report if needed.

policies.title: Medication Reminders and Self-Administration Assistance
state_specifics: Medically related activities include reminding clients to take medication and assisting with self-administration. Professional services are excluded.
Non-licensed staff do not administer medications, draw up insulin, or make medication decisions.
Training in medically related activities is part of the 40-hour program.
Report significant medication errors as incidents (SAF-02).
Document each reminder or assistance in the daily notes.

policies.title: Client Intake, Eligibility and Assessment
state_specifics: Record the initial contact date and the referral date, and screen for medical frailty.
Accept only clients whose services the agency can reasonably deliver.
Collect the responsible party's information and the physicians' names and numbers.
Complete the service agreement within the Rule .09(2)(b) deadline and the service plan within 7 working days.
Medicaid clients are referred through the Area Agency on Aging or the waiver case manager.

policies.title: Scheduling, Missed Visits and Continuity of Care
state_specifics: Keep a back-up caregiver list.
If an unexpected shortage prevents delivery, advise the client and refer them elsewhere if they want.
Document missed visits, the reason, and notice to the client and the case manager.
Do not use no-show penalties that conflict with the client's right to cancel.
Track late and missed visits in the QI program.

policies.title: Discharge, Transfer and Discontinuation of Services
state_specifics: The service plan includes a discharge plan.
Clients may cancel at any time; the agency refers clients elsewhere if it cannot continue service.
Give written notice with reasons and referral options for agency-initiated discharge.
Notify the payer or waiver case manager.
Keep the file at least 5 years from the last service.

policies.title: Coordination With Medicaid Waiver Programs (CCSP/SOURCE, ICWP, NOW/COMP)
state_specifics: Hold a current DCH PHCP license before serving as an in-home waiver provider (DAS HCBS 5300 § 208).
CCSP/SOURCE (waiver IDs 590/930) bill T1019 with TF/UC modifiers; ICWP (660) and NOW/COMP (680/681) bill T2025.
DCH handles enrollment, reimbursement and utilization review; DAS runs day-to-day CCSP operations. DBHDD manages NOW/COMP.
Follow the waiver service plan and case manager authorizations, and confirm whether payment is fee-for-service or through a CMO.
Never bill private-pay rates for authorized waiver services.

policies.title: Electronic Visit Verification and Timekeeping
state_specifics: EVV is required for Medicaid-financed personal care. Georgia's system is Netsmart Mobile Caregiver+.
Each visit records service type, recipient, provider, date, location and start/end time.
Georgia EVV Customer Support: (833) 483-5587.
HHCS claims with dates of service on or after 2026-09-14 must go through EVV; confirm the current date on the DCH EVV page.
Supervisors correct visits before billing; payroll hours must reconcile with EVV and daily notes.

policies.title: Background Checks, Fingerprint Determinations and Employee Registries
state_specifics: The owner must comply with Chapter 111-8-12 before a new license issues.
The administrator and each direct access employee need a satisfactory fingerprint records check determination before serving clients.
Check the OIG exclusion list at hire and monthly.
No credible evidence of abuse, neglect or exploitation.
Confirm with HFRD the exact process, since the GCHEXS process was not verified.

policies.title: Wage, Hour, Overtime and Travel Time Compliance
state_specifics: Agencies as third-party employers may not claim the companionship exemption from overtime. Confirm the current 29 CFR 552.109 status before finalizing.
Pay for travel between clients during the workday.
Federal minimum wage is $7.25 per hour.
Employ aides as W-2 employees.
Pay for orientation and the 40-hour training time.

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: Caregivers perform only the tasks in the service plan and within their training.
No gifts, loans, or handling of client money without authorization and bonding.
Keep client information confidential and respect the client's property and residence.
Report boundary violations to the supervisor.
Include annual evaluation of conduct in the performance review.

documents.title: Rules and Regulations for Private Home Care Providers, Subject 111-8-65 (Rules 111-8-65-.04 and .09 to .12 contain the written-policy and plan requirements)
documents.form_number: Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-65 (no DCH policy-checklist form number found)
documents.issuer: Georgia Department of Community Health (DCH), Healthcare Facility Regulation Division; published by the Georgia Secretary of State, Rules & Regulations of the State of Georgia
documents.version: Current text on rules.sos.ga.gov, retrieved 2026-10-14. Rule .09 was originally adopted eff. 3/12/2013 and has since been amended. The LII/Cornell copy of .09 is an older text, so the SOS text controls where they differ.
documents.how_used: I found no single DCH policy-review checklist or application packet for this license, so the regulation sections are used instead. Rules .04, .09, .10, .11 and .12 list the required written policies and procedures, and .03(s) adds a transport requirement. Rule .09(1), .09(2) and .09(4) text comes from the SOS page. The rest of .09 comes from the SOS page where it was not cut off, and from LII where it was cut off. Rules .10 and .11 come from LII plus SOS snippets. Rule .12 comes from LII search excerpts and is incomplete (see notes). Application, fee, ownership and background-check paperwork under .05 and .06 is excluded as non-policy content.

documents.title: DHS Division of Aging Services HCBS 5300 Manual Appendix E, Client Rights and Responsibilities (suggested form; waiver/CCSP context only)
documents.issuer: Georgia DHS Division of Aging Services
documents.how_used: Reference only, for waiver/CCSP providers. HCBS 5300 § 208.15 says providers must give clients a written copy of their rights and responsibilities. It is not a licensure checklist, and no items are drawn from it.

required_items.text: Each private home care provider shall have a governing body empowered and responsible to determine all policies and procedures and to ensure compliance with these rules.

Services Description. A provider shall establish and implement written policies and procedures that define the scope of private home care services it offers and the types of clients it serves. No provider shall provide services that are prohibited by these rules, the applicable legal authority, or other laws.
Service Agreements. No provider shall offer to provide a client any private home care services that it cannot reasonably expect to deliver in accordance with these rules.

A provider shall establish and implement policies and procedures for service agreements. All services provided to a client shall be based on a written service agreement entered into with the client or the client's responsible party, if applicable. The service agreement must include the following:
Date that provider makes initial contact with client for services;
Date of referral, i.e. the date on which the provider received a specific request to deliver private home care services to a particular client;
Description of services needed as stated by client or responsible party, if applicable;
Description of services to be provided and expected frequency and duration of services;
Charges for such services, and mechanisms for billing and payment of such charges;
Acknowledgment of receipt of a copy of client's rights and responsibilities as outlined at rule .12;
A telephone number of the provider that a client can call for information, questions, or complaints about services supplied by the provider;

The telephone number of the state licensing authority, i.e. the department, to call for information or questions about the provider concerning a violation of licensing requirements that was not resolved to the client's satisfaction by complaining to the provider;

Authorization from client or responsible party, if applicable, for access to client's personal funds when home management services are to be provided and when those services include assistance with bill paying or any activities, such as shopping, that involve access to or use of such funds; similarly approved authorization for use of client's motor vehicle when services to be provided include transport and escort services and when the client's personal vehicle will be used;

Signatures for the provider's representative and the client or responsible party, if applicable, and date signed; if a client or responsible party refuses to sign the agreement, such refusal shall be noted on the agreement with an explanation from the provider's representative.

For new clients, such initial service agreements shall be completed not later than the second visit to the client's residence to provide services if the second visit occurs on a different day from the first visit or not later than seven calendar days after services are initially provided in the residence, whichever is earlier.
If the provider is unable to complete the service agreement for good cause, the provider will document such reason(s) in the client's file.

Subsequent revisions to the initial service agreement may be handled by the provider noting in the client's record the specific changes in service (e.g. addition or deletion of service, changes in frequency, or duration, or charge for services, etc.) that will occur and that the change was discussed with and agreed to by the client and/or responsible party, as appropriate, who signed the initial agreement prior to the change in services occurring.

A client has the right to cancel any service agreement at any time and shall only be charged for services actually rendered prior to the time that the provider is notified of the cancellation. The provider may assess a reasonable charge for travel and staff time if notice of the cancellation of the service agreement is not provided in time to cancel the service prior to the provider's staff member arriving at the client's house to perform the service.
Administrator. The governing body shall appoint an administrator who shall have full authority and responsibility for the operation of the private home care provider.

Any administrator employed by the provider must meet the following minimum qualifications: 1. Obtain a satisfactory fingerprint records check determination in compliance with the Rules and Regulations for Criminal Background Checks, Chapter 111-8-12; 2. Participate in the orientation and training required by these rules; 3. Not have made any material false statements concerning qualifications requirements either to the department or the provider.

Client Records. A provider shall maintain a separate file containing all written records pertaining to the services provided for each client that it serves and the file shall contain the following: 1. Identifying information including name, address, telephone number, and responsible party, if any; 2. Current service agreement as described at rule .09(2); 3. Current service plan as described at rule .11; 4. Clinical and/or progress notes if the client is receiving nursing services that have been signed and dated by the staff providing the direct care; 5. Documentation of personal care tasks and companion or sitter tasks actually performed for the client; 6. Documentation of findings of home supervisory visits by the supervisor unless entered in service plan; 7. Any material reports from or about the client that relate to the care being provided to the client including items such as progress notes and problems reported by employees of the provider, communications with personal physicians or other health care providers, communications with family members or responsible parties, or similar items; 8. The names, addresses, and telephone numbers of the client's personal physicians, if any; and 9. Date and source of referral.

Retention and Confidentiality of Client Records. Written policies and procedures shall be established and implemented for the maintenance and security of client records specifying who shall supervise the maintenance of records, who shall have custody of records, to whom records may be released and for what purposes and how long the records will be retained.
At a minimum, all client records shall be retained for five years from the date of last service provided. The provider shall maintain the confidentiality of client records.

Employees of the provider shall not disclose or knowingly permit the disclosure of any information in a client record except to appropriate provider staff, the client, responsible party (if applicable), the client's physician or other health care provider, the department, other individuals authorized by the client in writing or by subpoena.

Personnel Records. A provider shall maintain separate written records for each employee and the records shall include the following: 1. Identifying information such as name, address, telephone number, and emergency contact person(s); 2. A five year employment history or a complete employment history if the person has not been employed five years; 3. Records of qualifications; 4. Records of health screenings, demonstrating compliance with the following: (i) Each provider shall have in place a health screening program designed to identify conditions that may place clients at risk for infection, injury, or improper care. The program shall include requirements and processes for initial, routine, and targeted health screenings of employees and contractors who interact with clients or conduct other activities with environmental impact. (ii) Screening for Tuberculosis (TB). Prior to starting work, all employees must be screened for TB in accordance with CDC guidance for baseline screening and testing for health care personnel. 5. Date of employment; 6. The person's job description or statements of the person's duties and responsibilities; 7. Documentation of orientation and training required by these rules; 8. Documentation of at least an annual performance evaluation; 9. Documentation of bonding if the employee performs home management services which permit unlimited access to the client's personal funds. (If bonding is provided through a universal coverage bond, evidence of bonding need not be maintained separately in each personnel folder.)

Reports of Complaints and Incidents. The provider shall maintain files of all documentation of complaints submitted pursuant to rule .12(2). A provider shall also maintain on file for a minimum of five years all incident reports or reports of unusual occurrences (e.g. falls, accidents, significant medication errors, etc.) that affect the health, safety, and welfare of its clients. Documentation required to be maintained shall include what actions, if any, the provider took to resolve clients' complaints and to address any incident reports or unusual occurrences required to be retained.

Staffing. The provider shall have sufficient numbers of qualified staff as required by these rules to provide the services specified in the service agreements with its clients. In the event that the provider becomes aware that it is unable to deliver the specified services to the client because of an unexpected staff shortage, the provider shall advise the client and refer the client to another provider if the client so desires.

All staff employed by a provider shall have included in their personnel records or files maintained by the particular provider a written evaluation that was performed within one year before or after the effective date of these rules. The written evaluation must reflect that the employee's performance of required job tasks was observed personally by a supervisor either by demonstration or observation and such performance was determined to be competent for all job tasks required to be performed. All staff hired by the provider must meet the following minimum qualifications: 1. Prior to serving as a direct access employee, obtain a satisfactory fingerprint records check determination in compliance with the Rules and Regulations for Criminal Background Checks, Chapter 111-8-12; 2. Participate in the orientation and training required by these rules; 3. Not have made any material false statements concerning qualifications requirements either to the department or the provider.

Nursing Personnel. Any persons employed by the provider to provide nursing services shall be licensed in Georgia in accordance with professional licensing laws and associated rules. Such persons may also provide any other types of private home care services offered by the provider.

Personal Care Assistant (PCA). The provider may have PCAs perform personal care tasks for clients. Such persons may also perform companion or sitter tasks for clients, but shall not provide nursing services unless qualified as stated in rule .09(5)(b) above.

Any PCA hired after the effective date of these rules shall have the following training and/or experience: (i) successful completion of a nurse aide training and competency evaluation program pursuant to the requirements of 42 CFR Part 483, Subpart D, as revised or recodified, if applicable; or (ii) successful completion of a competency examination for nurse aides recognized by the department; or (iii) successful completion of a health care or personal care credentialing program recognized and approved by the department; or (iv) successful completion or progress in the completion of a 40 hour training program provided by a private home care provider, which addresses at least the following areas: (I) Ambulation and transfer of clients, including positioning; (II) Assistance with bathing, toileting, grooming, shaving, dental care, dressing, and eating; (III) Basic first aide and CPR; (IV) Caring for clients with special conditions and needs so long as the services are within the scope of the tasks authorized to be performed by demonstration; (V) Home management; (VI) Home safety and sanitation; (VII) Infection control in the home; (VIII) Medically related activities to include the taking of vital signs; and (IX) Proper nutrition.
required_items.cite: Rule 111-8-65-.09(5)(c)1(i)-(iv)(I)-(IX) (LII text; SOS text was cut off here)

required_items.text: A training program described in rule .09(5)(c)1.(iv) must be conducted under the direction of a licensed registered professional nurse, or a health care professional with commensurate education and experience. Twenty hours of the program must be completed by the employee prior to serving clients and the additional twenty hours must be completed within six months of the date the training initially began. No PCA shall be assigned to perform a task for which training has not been completed and competency has not been determined. No PCA shall be assigned to care for a client with special conditions unless the PCA has received training and has demonstrated competency in performing such services related to such special conditions.

Companions or Sitters. The provider may have companions or sitters perform companion or sitter tasks for clients. 1. Such persons may not provide other private home care services to clients unless qualified as stated in rules .09(5)(b)and(c). 2. Any companion or sitter hired after the effective date of these rules must meet the following minimal requirements: (i) Be able to read and write, follow verbal and written instructions, and complete written reports and documents; (ii) Successfully complete training or demonstrate understanding and practical competency in the following areas: understanding the needs and characteristics of elderly, handicapped, or convalescing individuals; meal preparation and serving; transportation and escort services; housekeeping to include sanitation; home safety; handling medical emergencies in the home; and infection control.

Staff Training. Prior to working with clients, all employees hired or used on or after the effective date of these rules and who provide services to clients shall be oriented in accordance with these rules and shall thereafter receive additional training in accordance with these rules.

Orientation shall include instruction in: 1. The provider's written policies and procedures regarding its scope of services and the types of clients it serves (rule .09(1) and clients rights and responsibilities and complaints (rule .12), as well as other policies that are relevant to the employee's range of duties and responsibilities; 2. The employee's assigned duties and responsibilities; 3. Reporting client progress and problems to supervisory personnel and procedures for handling medical emergencies or other incidents that affect the delivery of services in accordance with the client's services plan; 4. The employee's obligation to report known exposure to tuberculosis and hepatitis to the employer.

Additional training consisting of a minimum of eight clock hours of training or instruction shall be provided annually for each employee after the first year of employment. Employees hired prior to the effective date of these rules are also required to receive eight clock hours of training or instruction annually beginning with the effective date of these rules. Such training or instruction shall be in subjects that relate to the employee's assigned duties and responsibilities.

Contracted Services. If a provider arranges with independent contractors, individuals, or agents for them to provide any authorized private home care services on behalf of the provider in any way, such arrangements shall be set forth in writing detailing the services to be provided. The provider must assure that the independent contractor, individual, or agent supplying the services follow the provisions of these rules and are qualified to provide the services. The services must be supervised, as outlined in rule .10(2) (Supervision of Services), by a supervisor of the licensed provider.

Nursing Services. If a provider provides nursing services, such services shall be provided by a licensed registered professional nurse or a licensed practical nurse under the direction of a supervisor as required by these rules. Such services shall be provided in accordance with the scope of nursing practice laws and associated rules, and the client's service plan. 1. Nursing services shall include the following: (i) Regularly assess the nursing needs of the client; (ii) Participate in the establishment and implementation of the client's service plan; (iii) Provide nursing services as needed and in accordance with the client's service plan; (iv) Report problems and progress of client to supervisory personnel or the client's personal physician.

Personal Care Tasks. If a provider provides personal care tasks, such tasks, at a minimum, shall be performed by a qualified PCA under the direction of a supervisor as required by these rules, and in accordance with the client's service plan. In addition to following the service plan, a PCA must report on the personal care needs of the client, on changes in the client's condition, and on any observed problems that affect the client. Licensed nurses are also authorized to perform personal care tasks.

Companion or Sitter Tasks. If a provider provides companion or sitter tasks, such tasks, at a minimum, shall be performed by a qualified companion or sitter under the direction of a qualified supervisor as required by these rules, and in accordance with the client's service plan. In addition to following the service plan, a companion or sitter must report on the needs of the client, on changes in the client's condition, and on any observed problems that affect the client.

Supervision of Services. Services shall be supervised by qualified staff of the provider. Each staff member providing services to a client shall be evaluated in writing by his or her supervisor, at least annually, either through direct observation or demonstration, on the job tasks the staff member is required to perform. No supervisor shall knowingly permit an employee who has been exposed to tuberculosis or hepatitis or diagnosed with the same to provide services to clients until it is determined that the employee is not contagious.

Supervision of Nursing Services. If a provider provides nursing services, it shall employ fully licensed Georgia registered professional nurse to supervise the provision of such services and the employees who provide the services. Such supervisor may perform other duties provided he or she is able to fulfill the supervisory responsibilities described in these rules. A supervisor shall complete the client's service plan in accordance with rule .11 and in coordination with the appropriate staff who will be providing the client's services.

Supervision of Personal Care Tasks. If a provider offers personal care task services, the provider shall employ supervisor(s) that have been determined to be qualified by education, training and experience to supervise the provision of such tasks in accordance with accepted standards of care. A licensed registered professional or practical nurse shall supervise the provision of personal care tasks for clients determined to be medically frail or medically compromised. If such supervision is provided by a licensed practical nurse, the licensed practical nurse shall report to a licensed registered professional nurse who will continue to be responsible for the development and management of the service plan. Such supervisor may perform other duties provided he or she is able to fulfill the supervisory responsibilities described in these rules.

The appropriate supervisor as specified in these rules shall complete the client's service plan in accordance with rule .11 and in coordination with the appropriate staff who will be providing the client's services. For clients who are determined to be medically frail or compromised, a licensed registered professional nurse shall complete the initial service plan. Subsequent revisions to the service plan may be made by a licensed practical nurse who is supervising the provision of personal care tasks services to the client. Revisions made by the licensed practical nurse will be reviewed in a timely manner by the provider's licensed registered professional nurse ultimately responsible for the management of the client's care.

The appropriate supervisor shall make a supervisory home visit to each client's residence at least every 92 days, starting from date of initial service in a residence or as the level of care requires to ensure that the client's needs are met. The visit shall include an assessment of the client's general condition, vital signs, a review of the progress being made, the problems encountered by the client and the client's satisfaction with the services being delivered by the provider's staff. Such supervision shall also include observations about the appropriateness of the level of services being offered. Routine quarterly supervisory visits shall be made in the client's residence and shall be documented in the client's file or service plan.

Supervision of Companion or Sitter Tasks. If a provider provides companion or sitter tasks, supervision of such tasks shall be provided by a qualified supervisor (e.g. registered professional nurse, licensed practical nurse, the administrator, or any other staff member assigned responsibility for supervision of the delivery of care.)

The appropriate supervisor, as specified in these rules, shall complete the client's service plan in accordance with rule .11 and in coordination with the appropriate staff who will be providing the client's services.

The appropriate supervisor shall make a supervisory home visit to each client's residence at least every 122 days starting from date of initial service in the residence or when the provider receives a complaint concerning services and the complaint raises a serious question concerning the services being delivered. The visit shall include an assessment of the client's general condition, a review of the progress being made, the problems encountered by the client and the client's satisfaction with the services being delivered by the provider's staff. Such supervision shall also include observations about the appropriateness of the level of services being offered. Routine supervisory visits shall be made in the client's residence. All supervisory visits shall be documented in the client's file or service plan.

When employees or subcontractors are performing personal care tasks for clients who are medically frail or medically compromised in the clients' residences, the provider shall have a representative on call and accessible who shall be able to contact a nurse supervisor by telephone or other means to provide appropriate consultation to the employees or subcontractors concerning responding to the clients' medical needs.

Documentation of Home Care Services Provided. A provider shall establish and implement written policies and procedures for documenting the services actually performed for its clients each day. Such documentation shall be incorporated into the client's file in accordance with rule .09(4)(a).

Quality Improvement Program. The provider must have and maintain documentation reflecting that there is an effective quality improvement program that continuously monitors the performance of the program itself and client outcomes to ensure that the care provided to the clients meets acceptable standards of care and complies with the minimum requirements set forth in these rules. At a minimum, the quality improvement program must document the receipt and resolution (if possible) of client complaints, problems with care identified and corrective actions taken.

Service Plan Content. A provider shall establish and implement written policies and procedures for service planning. A written plan of service shall be established in collaboration with the client and the responsible party, if applicable, and the client's personal physician if the services to be provided are nursing services and the client has a personal physician.

Service plans shall be completed by the service supervisor within seven working days after services are initially provided in the residence. Service plans for nursing services shall be reviewed and updated at least every sixty-two days. [LII's version adds: 'Other service plans shall be reviewed and updated at the time of each supervisory visit.']
A provider shall establish and implement written policies and procedures regarding the rights and responsibilities of clients, and the handling and resolution of complaints.

Such policies and procedures shall include a written notice of rights and responsibilities which shall be provided to each client or responsible party, if applicable, when the service agreement described in rule .09(2) is completed. The required notice shall include the following items:
Right to be informed about plan of service and to participate in the planning;
Right to be promptly and fully informed of any changes in the plan of service;
Right to accept or refuse services;
Right to be fully informed of the charges for services;
Right to be informed of the name, business telephone number and business address of the person supervising the services and how to contact that person;

Right to be informed of the complaint procedures and the right to submit complaints without fear of discrimination or retaliation and to have them investigated by the provider within a reasonable period of time. The complaint procedure provided shall include the name, business address and telephone number of the person designated by the provider to handle complaints and questions;
Right of confidentiality of client record;
Right to have property and residence treated with respect;

Right to receive a written notice of the address and telephone number of the state licensing authority, i.e. the department, which further explains that the department is charged with the responsibility of licensing the provider and investigating client complaints which appear to violate licensing regulations;

Right to obtain a copy of the provider's most recent completed report of licensure inspection from the provider upon w[request] (text cut off in the retrieved excerpt; the rest of .12(2)(j) and any later items such as client responsibilities were not retrieved and must be checked against the official page)

Transport and escort services: if the mode of transportation is not owned by the client and is operated by an employee of the provider, the provider shall either obtain a signed waiver by the client of any claims for damages arising out of the operation of the vehicle or make reasonable efforts to insure that there is current motor vehicle insurance that will provide medical coverage for the client, in the event that the vehicle is involved in an accident causing injuries to the client. (Definition with an operational requirement; relevant if transport is offered.)

Home management: any employee that is authorized unlimited access to a client's personal funds for home management shall be bonded through the provider. (Definition with an operational requirement; ties to .09(4)(c)9.)

official.notes: I found no state-issued policy checklist form, policy-manual template or plan-of-operation instruction sheet for the Georgia private home care license. This answer is therefore built from the regulation, as the task allows. Rule 111-8-65-.06(1) only requires a description of the services to be offered and the geographic area to be served, on DCH forms. The written policies are checked on inspection under Rule .08, and a provisional license may be issued to let a new provider show its procedures comply (Rule .05(1)(c)). Rule .08(4) requires a written plan of correction within 10 days of receiving an inspection report that cites violations. A reasonable manual layout is one tab per rule section: .09(1) scope of services; .09(2) service agreement and cancellation; .09(3) and .09(5) administrator, staffing and qualifications; .09(4) client and personnel records plus the retention and confidentiality policy; .09(6) orientation and annual training; .09(7) contractor agreements; .10 supervision, daily documentation and quality improvement; .11 service planning; .12 client rights, complaints and the notice of rights. Rules .09(4)(b), .10(3), .11(1) and .12(1) say 'written policies and procedures' explicitly. The rest of .09 and .10 are operating requirements that policies must address. The rules do not list separate policies for medication, abuse reporting, emergency or disaster plans, discipline, menus or theft and loss. The only related items are .09(4)(d) (incident and unusual-occurrence reports), .09(6)(a)3 (handling medical emergencies), .10(2)(d) (on-call nurse consultation), .03(g) (bonding), .09(2)(a)9 (authorization for access to client funds or vehicle) and .03(s) (transport waiver or insurance). Waiver programs (CCSP/SOURCE) additionally require a current DCH PHCP license under HCBS 5300 § 208, and the DAS client rights form (Appendix E) is only a suggested form. Data-quality caveats: (1) The SOS page cut off partway through .09(5)(c)1, so the rest of .09(5)(c)-(7) comes from the LII copy of the rule. LII's .09(3)(a), .09(4)(c)4 and .09(5)(a) are older versions, so I used the SOS wording for those. (2) For .10, .11 and .12 the SOS rule pages could not be fetched. Those come from the LII pages and search excerpts. .11(2)'s 62-day nursing-plan review appears only in an SOS excerpt, and .12(2)(j) onward was cut off. (3) I could not open the DCH Private Home Care Program page, so I could not confirm whether it posts an application packet or checklist. (4) A proposed revision of Rule .03 (HB 183, independent contractor limits) was listed in the inputs but adoption was not verified, so it is not reflected here. A third-party site (homecareagencypolicies.com) also says the written-policy requirements sit in .09, .10 and .11. That site is not an official source.
